code.pseudocode: The prior is what we believe before seeing the evidence.
Observe the evidence: the email contains 'free'.
The likelihood is how likely the evidence is if the email is spam.

steps.label: The likelihood: evidence given the cause

code.pseudocode: We know P(free | spam) but want P(spam | free). Bayes' rule reverses the condition.
code.python:
# known:  P(free | spam) = 0.6
# wanted: P(spam | free)
# Bayes: P(spam | free) = P(free | spam) * P(spam) / P(free)
print('reverse the condition')

code.pseudocode: P(free) adds up how often 'free' appears from every possible cause.
code.python:
prior = 0.4        # P(spam)
like_spam = 0.6    # P(free | spam)
like_ham = 0.1     # P(free | not spam)
evidence = like_spam * prior + like_ham * (1 - prior)
print(round(evidence, 2))   # 0.3

prior = 0.4        # P(spam)
like_spam = 0.6    # P(free | spam)
like_ham = 0.1     # P(free | not spam)
evidence = like_spam * prior + like_ham * (1 - prior)
posterior = like_spam * prior / evidence
print(round(posterior, 2))   # 0.8

code.pseudocode: Compare the prior with the posterior.
code.python:
prior = 0.4        # P(spam)
like_spam = 0.6    # P(free | spam)
like_ham = 0.1     # P(free | not spam)
evidence = like_spam * prior + like_ham * (1 - prior)
posterior = like_spam * prior / evidence
print(prior, round(posterior, 2))   # 0.4 0.8

code.pseudocode: Compute a posterior for each class and predict the larger one.
code.python:
prior = 0.4        # P(spam)
like_spam = 0.6    # P(free | spam)
like_ham = 0.1     # P(free | not spam)
evidence = like_spam * prior + like_ham * (1 - prior)
posterior = {'spam': like_spam * prior / evidence,
             'not spam': like_ham * (1 - prior) / evidence}
print({k: round(v, 2) for k, v in posterior.items()})   # {'spam': 0.8, 'not spam': 0.2}
print(max(posterior, key=posterior.get))   # spam
